summary: A 1939 three-story fire lookout near Annette in Kern County, built by the county fire department on private land; the register says its roof has since blown off.

facts.design: Three-story cab, per the FFLA California listing; the register says the design is unique to Kern County
facts.status_note: Standing but in serious decay; the register says the roof has blown off

staffing.status: Lookout crew responding to fires in 1954

access.note: Register lists the lookout as privately owned. No visiting information found.

facts.agency: Privately owned land; Kern County Fire Department (cooperator)

events.note: Constructed by the Kern County Fire Department
Lookout spotted a 400-acre grass fire near Cottonwood Pass in July
County leases part of a private parcel for 15 years for the station
Lookout crew responds to a grass fire and a storehouse fire in August
Structure generally intact during a visit
Register text says the roof has since blown off and the structure is in serious decay; date of the damage not given

corrections.current: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).
corrections.proposed: The tower still stands, but the register says its roof has blown off and it is in serious decay.
corrections.why: The NHLR detail page says the roof has blown off. It does not say the cab is gone. The FFLA California index I could read lists it as Standing* with a 3-Story Cab and no cab-gone note.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as standing with a three-story cab. The register says the roof blew off and the structure is in serious decay, and does not mention the cab. The claim that the cab is gone could not be checked.

notes_for_editor: Brief status_note ('cab is gone', FFLA) is not verified: the cached FFLA California index shows Standing* and 3-Story Cab with no note text, and the register says only that the roof blew off. The Kern County Fire Department Facebook post could not be read. The 1940 lease is the only ownership history, and the current owner is unknown. The 1954 fire items are the only staffing evidence.
